assessmentPlatform: Standard Tech Assessment (HackerRank / CodeSignal / LeetCode / Live Editor)

stages.name: Technical Screening & Online Assessment
stages.format: Timed online algorithmic challenge (typically 2 problems in 60-90 minutes)
rubricTraps: Inefficient Big-O time complexity causing timeout on large test sets
Edge case blindspots (boundary numbers, nulls, empty collections)
Overcomplicating the solution when a direct two-pointer or hash map approach suffices

stages.name: Core Algorithms & Data Structures
stages.format: Live interactive technical interview (45-60 minutes) with whiteboard or shared IDE
rubricTraps: Coding before verbally verifying the approach with the interviewer
Silent thinking without sharing reasoning or trade-offs
Messy variable naming and lack of modular helper decomposition
Failing to analyze time and space complexity with exact Big-O justification

stages.name: System Fundamentals & Behavioral Competency
stages.format: System design / architecture discussion and STAR method behavioral evaluation (45-60 minutes)
rubricTraps: Diving into microservices buzzwords without establishing clear throughput or capacity requirements
Ignoring database trade-offs (SQL vs NoSQL, consistency vs availability)
Vague answers to behavioral questions lacking concrete actions or measurable impact
Inability to reflect honestly on mistakes or technical friction
coreTopics: API Design & Web Protocols (REST, HTTP status codes)

behavioralFramework.name: STAR Behavioral Framework
sampleQuestions: Describe a technically difficult bug or outage you diagnosed and resolved under pressure.
Tell me about a time you had a technical disagreement with a teammate and how you reached consensus.
Walk me through a project where requirements shifted mid-stream and how you managed the changes.
What is an engineering decision you made that you would do differently in hindsight?
